I am 68 years old and have farmed these lands in Quzhou my whole life. Over the decades, I have watched the China Agricultural University professors work in our county, and because I attended high school—the highest education among my peers—I have always paid close attention to their recommendations. I do not chase risky crops. The North China Plain gives us one reliable harvest of winter wheat and one of summer maize on the same parcel of land, and that double-cropping system is what puts steady grain in my storage and cash in my pocket. Wheat has a government minimum purchase price and a small subsidy, so it anchors my family's food security. Maize follows immediately after the June wheat harvest; the market is always there for feed and starch factories.

This spring, the winter wheat I sowed last October is already greening up. I will manage it carefully: rotary tillage was done before sowing, and now I will irrigate four times—overwintering water was already applied, and I will add jointing, heading, and grain-filling irrigations as the weather demands. I use an improved wheat variety like Jimai or Shijiazhuang because it resists lodging and gives about 550 kg per mu if the weather cooperates. For fertilizer, I have learned that more nitrogen is not always better; I will apply about 14 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu, split between basal compound fertilizer and a top-dressing at the green-up stage. I will spray pesticides three times—once for weeds and twice for insects and fungi.

After the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant hybrid maize the same day, using a no-tillage seeder. Time is short between crops, and no-tillage protects the soil moisture. I will choose a hybrid like Zhengdan 958, which is proven here. Maize needs roughly 16 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu, applied mostly as basal compound fertilizer with a side-dressing of urea at the large trumpet stage. I will irrigate twice—at jointing and at flowering—because summer rains are unpredictable. Two pesticide applications will control weeds and corn borers. I expect about 600 kg per mu from the maize.

My land is 8 mu. I keep it all in this rotation because diversifying into vegetables or cotton brings price risk and heavier labor that my old body does not want anymore.
